package_info.package_versions: Versions affected by SunBurst attack (late 2019–2020, e.g., 2019.4 HF 5, 2020.2, 2020.2 HF 1)
package_info.why_malicious: The SolarWinds Orion update was compromised to include the SunBurst backdoor, which enabled attackers to gain persistent, covert access to customer environments, exfiltrate sensitive data, and facilitate further intrusions. The malicious code was signed and distributed as part of a trusted software update, making detection difficult and enabling widespread supply chain compromise.

execution_context.file_location: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (maliciously modified DLL in Orion update package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At service startup and periodically at runtime, the code checks for a suitable environment, delays execution to evade detection, then beacons system information to a hardcoded C2 domain (avsvmcloud.com). Upon receiving commands, it executes them and exfiltrates the results, enabling remote control and data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code introduces covert network communications to an external domain, delays execution to evade detection, and enables remote command execution and data exfiltration, all of which are hallmarks of backdoor malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Orion DLLs should not contain code that beacons to external domains, executes remote commands, or exfiltrates data. Such behavior is not required for normal network monitoring or management.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools may contact cloud APIs, but only to trusted, documented endpoints and never for arbitrary command execution.
key_indicators: Remote command execution and data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is inserted into the Orion update and signed with SolarWinds' certificate.
Customers install the compromised update, loading the malicious DLL into their environment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes on customer systems

attack_chain.action: Malicious code performs environment checks, delays execution, and beacons to the C2 domain.
Upon receiving commands, the malware executes them and exfiltrates sensitive data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data theft and potential lateral movement

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from Orion servers to avsvmcloud.com or similar C2 domains
Environment checks to evade sandboxes or analysis
Remote command execution capabilities in monitoring software
file_indicators: Unexpected changes in signed DLLs within Orion installation directory
Presence of unknown or suspicious DLLs loaded by Orion services
network_indicators: Connections to avsvmcloud.com and related C2 infrastructure
Outbound HTTPS traffic from Orion servers to unknown domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Orion server processes for unexpected outbound network connections, especially to avsvmcloud.com or similar domains. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized changes to signed DLLs in the Orion installation directory. Analyze loaded DLLs for suspicious logic such as randomized delays, environment checks, and remote command execution. Correlate with threat intelligence on known C2 domains and indicators of compromise from the SunBurst campaign.
